In his saying «فمن عفا وأصلح فأجره على الله إنه لا يحب الظالمين» there is a lofty art, which is also tahdhīb, for in retaliation one can scarcely be safe from exceeding the evil and from aggression, especially in the state of seething, boiling and flaring of zeal; and in this is an answer to whoever asks what is meant by mentioning wrongdoing after pardon, when retaliation is not wrongdoing. Of this Khosrow-brocade is the saying of the Exalted «وإذا أذقنا الإنسان منّا رحمة فرح بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدّمت أيديهم فإن الإنسان كفور»: He did not say «فإنه كفور», in order to register against this kind that it is marked with ingratitude for blessings, as will come shortly. Of it also is «وقال الذين آمنوا إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم»: He put «الظالمين» in the place of the pronoun, which by right should have referred back to the noun of «إن», so that it would be said «ألا إنهم في عذاب مقيم», and this overt noun came as a registering against them in the tongue of their wrongdoing; and this is among the badīʿ that soars above the capacities of the innovators.

* Benefits:
Omitting the linking fāʾ: The linking fāʾ is sometimes omitted, rarely, as in the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb when he asked him about a lost item: "If its owner comes (fine), otherwise make use of it" (recorded by al-Bukhārī); or out of poetic necessity, as in the saying of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها ... والشر بالشرّ عند الله مثلان
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah thanks them; and evil by evil are, with Allah, two alike.)
He meant «فالله يشكرها». It is related of al-Mubarrad that he forbade that absolutely, but it occurs often, as in the saying:
ومن لا يزل ينقاد للغي والصبا ... سيلفى على طول السلامة نادما
(Whoever continues to be led by error and folly, will be found, despite long safety, a regretful man.)
He meant «فسيلفى».

dervis-irab:44-46.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; «من» is conditional, in the position of accusative as a fronted object; «يضلل» is the protasis and the Majestic Name is its agent; the fāʾ is a link; «ما» is negative; «له» is a fronted khabar; «من» is a redundant preposition and «ولي» is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ; «من بعده» is an adjective of «ولي». (وَتَرَى الظَّالِمِينَ لَمَّا رَأَوُا الْعَذابَ يَقُولُونَ هَلْ إِلى مَرَدٍّ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ) It has preceded that the address is general, including everyone for whom seeing is possible. «ترى» is a nominative imperfect verb, the seeing being visual; «الظالمين» is a direct object; «لما» is temporal or a link; «رأوا العذاب»: a past verb, an agent and an object; the clause «يقولون» is circumstantial; «هل» is an interrogative particle; «إلى مرد», i.e. a return, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; «من» is a redundant preposition and «سبيل» is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ. (وَتَراهُمْ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْها خاشِعِينَ مِنَ الذُّلِّ يَنْظُرُونَ مِنْ طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ) «وتراهم» is conjoined to «ترى»; the clause «يعرضون» is circumstantial, because the seeing is visual as preceded; the wāw is the deputy agent; «عليها» is attached to «يعرضون», and the pronoun in «عليها» refers to the Fire, which the word «العذاب» indicates; «خاشعين» is a second ḥāl; «من الذل» is attached to «خاشعين», i.e. on account of it, and it may be attached to «ينظرون»; «من طرف» is attached to «ينظرون» and «خفي» is an adjective of «طرف». Is «الطرف» meant as the eye or as the maṣdar? Both suit the context. In al-Mukhtār: "ṭarafa baṣarahu, of the pattern ḍaraba, when he closed one eyelid upon the other, and the single instance is ṭarfa; one says 'faster than the blink of an eye'." More discussion of this skilful, embodied depiction will come in the section of Rhetoric. (وَقالَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ الْخاسِرِينَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) The wāw is a conjunction; «قال الذين آمنوا»: a verb, an agent and a ṣila; «إن» and its noun, and «الذين» is its khabar; «خسروا أنفسهم»: a verb, an agent and an object, and the clause is a ṣila; «أهليهم» is conjoined to «أنفسهم»; «يوم القيامة» is an adverbial attached to «خسروا»; al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be attached to «قال», i.e. "they will say on the Day of Resurrection when they see them in that condition". (أَلا إِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ فِي عَذابٍ مُقِيمٍ) «ألا» is a particle of alerting; «إن» and its noun, and «في عذاب» is its khabar; «مقيم» is an adjective; the clause is part of the content of the saying of Allah the Exalted, and it may also be part of their speech. (وَما كانَ لَهُمْ مِنْ أَوْلِياءَ يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is negative; «كان» is a past defective verb; «لهم» is the fronted khabar of «كان»; «من» is a redundant preposition and «أولياء» is genitive by «من» in form, in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of «كان»; the clause «ينصرونهم» is an adjective of «أولياء» and «من دون الله» is a ḥāl. (وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; «من» is conditional, in the position of accusative as a fronted object of «يضلل»; «يضلل» is the protasis and the Majestic Name its agent; the fāʾ links the apodosis; «ما» is negative; «له» is a fronted khabar; «من» is a redundant preposition and «سبيل» is genitive by «من» in form, nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ; what is meant by «السبيل» here is the way that leads to the truth in this world, or to Paradise in the next.

* Rhetoric:
In his saying «ينظرون من طرف خفي» there is a skilful embodiment and a wondrous depiction of one who stands before the death awaiting him, with the sword drawn above his head: he flutters his eyelids and moves them with a weak, hidden movement that lets him steal a glance; for whoever looks at a hateful matter finds its affair dreadful and turns his sight away from it, yet he cannot restrain himself from casting a swift glance at what he hates and expects to befall.

dervis-irab:47-48.t:
* I'rab:
(اسْتَجِيبُوا لِرَبِّكُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا مَرَدَّ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ) «استجيبوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; «لربكم» is attached to it, i.e. answer Him with divine oneness and worship; «من قبل» is also attached to «استجيبوا»; «أن» and what is in its scope is annexed to the adverbial; «يوم» is the agent; «لا» is the lā of generic negation and «مرد» is its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa, and «له» is its khabar; «من الله» is attached to «مرد» because it is a maṣdar mīmī (a maṣdar with prefixed mīm); the clause is an adjective of «يوم». Some allowed attaching «من الله» to «يأتي», i.e. "before there comes from Allah a day that no one is allowed to turn back". (ما لَكُمْ مِنْ مَلْجَإٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ نَكِيرٍ) «ما» is negative and «لكم» a fronted khabar; «من ملجإ»: «من» is a redundant preposition and «ملجإ» is genitive in form and nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ; «يومئذ» is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl; «ما لكم من نكير» is conjoined to «ما لكم من ملجإ». There is disagreement over the meaning of «النكير»: it is said to mean denial (inkār), as if it were a maṣdar of «أنكر» contrary to analogy; al-Asās was content with saying: "so-and-so was reviled and had no nakīr (rebuttal)"; in al-Qāmūs there is the following: "nakira fulān al-amr, like fariḥa, nakran with fatḥa on the kāf, and nukran and nukūran with ḍamma on both, and nakīran", citing it as a maṣdar of «نكر»; in al-Tahdhīb: "«النكير» is the noun of the denial (inkār) whose meaning is change"; for that reason al-Zamakhsharī pieced the meaning together from all the meanings, saying:
"«النكير» is denial, i.e. you have no escape from the punishment, and you cannot deny anything of what you committed and what was recorded in the pages of your deeds." Al-Zajjāj said: "Its meaning is that they cannot deny the sins to which they are made to stand." (فَإِنْ أَعْرَضُوا فَما أَرْسَلْناكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظاً) The fāʾ is resumptive; «إن» is conditional; «أعرضوا» is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, the wāw being the agent; the fāʾ is a link; «ما» is negative; «أرسلناك»: a verb, an agent and an object; «عليهم» is attached to «حفيظا», and «حفيظا» is a ḥāl; the meaning is "We sent you to compel them to follow what you brought them". The better view is that the apodosis is omitted and the fāʾ is a conjunction to the omitted apodosis, implied in a way suited to the context, i.e. "so do not grieve and do not try to compel them". (إِنْ عَلَيْكَ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ) «إن» is negative; «عليك» is a fronted khabar; «إلا» is a particle of restriction and «البلاغ» a postponed mubtadaʾ. It is said this is abrogated by the verses commanding jihad. (وَإِنَّا إِذا أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنَّا رَحْمَةً فَرِحَ بِها) The wāw is a conjunction; «إن» and its noun; «إذا» is a future adverbial containing the sense of a condition, and the clause «أذقناه» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; «الإنسان» is a direct object; «منا» is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «رحمة» and was fronted; «رحمة» is a direct object, i.e. a favour; the clause «فرح بها» has no position because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition, and the conditional clause is the khabar of «إن». (وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ فَإِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ كَفُورٌ) Conjoined to what precedes; «إن» is conditional and «تصبهم» is the protasis; the pronoun refers to «الإنسان» taken as a genus, so he made it plural by meaning; «سيئة» is the agent of «تصبهم»; «بما» is attached to «تصبهم»; «ما» is a relative and the clause «قدمت أيديهم» is a ṣila, the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. «قدمته»; he expressed it with "the hands" because most deeds are performed with them; the fāʾ is a link, or the reason for the implied apodosis, the implied form being "if an evil befalls them they forget the favour immediately"; «إن», its noun and its khabar. We have already mentioned in the section of Rhetoric noted above the secret of the overt noun's occurring in place of the pronoun, i.e. «فإنه كفور».

dervis-irab:49-53.t:
* I'rab:
(لِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ) A resumptive speech to show the breadth of His dominion, Glory be to Him; «الملك» with ḍamma is taking hold of a thing and disposing of it as one wills. «لله» is a fronted khabar and «ملك السموات والأرض» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause «يخلق» is a ḥāl; «ما» is the direct object of «يخلق» and the clause «يشاء» is a ṣila. (يَهَبُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ إِناثاً وَيَهَبُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ الذُّكُورَ) «يهب» is a nominative imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "He", referring to Allah the Exalted; «لمن» is attached to «يهب» and the clause «يشاء» is a ṣila; «إناثا» is a direct object; «ويهب لمن يشاء الذكور» is conjoined to the preceding clause; the clause «يهب لمن يشاء» is a badal of the clause «يخلق ما يشاء», a detailed substitute for a general one. (أَوْ يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْراناً وَإِناثاً وَيَجْعَلُ مَنْ يَشاءُ عَقِيماً إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ) «أو» is a conjunction; «يزوجهم» is an imperfect verb with a latent agent referring to Him, Glory be to Him, and an object; «ذكرانا وإناثا» is a second direct object of «يزوجهم», the verb being given the sense of making (taṣyīr), i.e. He makes his children males and females, by the evidence of what follows; Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Khaṭīb chose to parse «ذكرانا وإناثا» as two ḥāls. «ويجعل من يشاء عقيما» is conjoined to what precedes, and «عقيما» is necessarily a second direct object; «إن» and its noun; «عليم» is its first khabar and «قدير» its second khabar. More discussion of this verse will come in the section of Rhetoric. (وَما كانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحْياً أَوْ مِنْ وَراءِ حِجابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا) The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to show how Allah speaks to His servants; «ما» is negative; «كان» is a past defective verb; «لبشر» is the fronted khabar of «كان»; «أن» and its accusative verb are its noun; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «وحيا» is a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; «أو» is a conjunction; «من وراء حجاب» is attached to an implied element conjoined to the implied element that governs «وحيا», i.e. "except that Allah speaks from behind a veil" or "making Himself heard from behind a veil"; «أو» is a conjunction; «يرسل» is conjoined to a pure noun not construed with a verb, which is his saying «وحيا», as though He had said "except as one who reveals or sends", or "that He reveal a revelation or send a messenger". This verse has occupied the exegetes and grammarians, and we shall bring you in the section of Benefits a detailed discussion on it. (فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذْنِهِ ما يَشاءُ إِنَّهُ عَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ) «فيوحي» is conjoined to «يرسل»; both have been read with raising as a resumption, i.e. "so He sends and reveals"; «بإذنه» is attached to «يوحي»; the waḥy is inspiration and the swift signal; «ما» is a direct object and the clause «يشاء» is a ṣila; «إن», its noun and its two khabars. (وَكَذلِكَ أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ رُوحاً مِنْ أَمْرِنا) The kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. like Our revelation to others than you; «إليك» is attached to «أوحينا»; «روحا» is a direct object; «من أمرنا» is an adjective of «روحا», and it is said a ḥāl, with «من» partitive, i.e. this spirit, which is the Qur'an, being part of what We reveal to you, because what is revealed to him is not restricted to the Qur'an. (ما كُنْتَ تَدْرِي مَا الْكِتابُ وَلَا الْإِيمانُ) The clause is a ḥāl from the kāf in «إليك»; «ما» is interrogative, suspended (muʿallaqa) so that «تدري» does not act, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; «الكتاب» is the khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative, standing in for the two objects of «تدري»; «ولا الإيمان» is conjoined to «الكتاب». (وَلكِنْ جَعَلْناهُ نُوراً نَهْدِي بِهِ مَنْ نَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِنا) The wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction; «لكن» is a particle of rectification, inoperative; «جعلناه»: a verb, an agent and an object; «نورا» is a second direct object; the clause «نهدي به» is an adjective of «نورا»; «من» is a direct object and the clause «نشاء» is a ṣila; «من عبادنا» is a ḥāl. (وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِي إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; «إن» and its noun, and the shifted lām; the clause «تهدي» is the khabar; the object of «تهدي» is omitted, i.e. every responsible person; «إلى صراط مستقيم» is attached to «تهدي». (صِراطِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) «صراط الله» is a badal of the first, a definite substitute for an indefinite; «الذي» is an adjective of «الله»; «له» is a fronted khabar and «ما» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «في السموات» is attached to an omitted element as the ṣila; «وما في الأرض» is conjoined to «ما في السموات». (أَلا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَصِيرُ الْأُمُورُ) «ألا» is a particle of alerting; «إلى الله» is attached to «تصير»; «الأمور» is the agent; what is meant by "becoming" here is permanence.

* Rhetoric:
These verses might take in what equals the pages that the whole sūra has taken up, but we shall be brief as far as possible while avoiding impairment. In his saying «يهب لمن يشاء إناثا ويهب لمن يشاء الذكور أو يزوّجهم» there is the art of soundness of division (ṣiḥḥat al-taqsīm), which has been touched on before: it is the speaker's exhausting all the parts of the meaning he has embarked upon, so that nothing of it is left out. For He, Glory be to Him, either singles out the servant with the gift of females, or with the gift of males, or with both together, or gives him nothing; so soundness of division occurs in this verse in the order that eloquence calls for, which is moving in the composition and arrangement of the speech from the lower to the higher: He put first the gift of females, moved to the gift of males, then to the gift of both together; in every part of the bestowal He used the word "gift", and singled out the sense of deprivation by postponing it, because His favouring His servants is more important to Him, and putting the more important first is necessary in all eloquent speech. The verse is brought only to reckon with the favours; He mentioned deprivation only so that praise might be completed by power over withholding as He is praised for giving, so that it is known that there is none to withhold what He gave and none to give what He withheld; and He turned from the word "deprivation" and "withholding" to a word that is its follower and companion, which is the word "making" (jaʿl). The like of it will come in Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa, with more detail; see it there.
Besides, there is the ṭibāq (antithesis) which is not hidden, as has often been discussed before.

* Benefits:
1- Before we give you an important grammatical rule, we give what the leading exegetes and grammarians said on the i'rab of his saying «وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا» (the verse).
Here is a summary of what al-Zamakhsharī said:
It is not right for any human being that Allah speak to him except in three ways:
1- Either by way of revelation (waḥy), which is inspiration and casting into the heart or in a dream.
2- Or by making him hear His speech, which He creates in some body, without the hearer seeing who speaks to him, because He in His essence is not seen.
3- Or by sending him a messenger from among the angels.
Until he says: "«وحيا» and «أن يرسل» are two maṣdars standing in the place of a ḥāl, because «أن يرسل» is in the sense of «إرسالا», and «من وراء حجاب» is an adverbial also standing in place of a ḥāl, as in his saying, the Exalted, «وعلى جنوبهم»; and the implied form is: it is not right that He speak to anyone except as one who reveals, or makes himself heard from behind a veil, or sends" until he says: "As for the one who makes «وحيا» in the sense of «أن يوحي» and conjoins «يرسل» to it, on the meaning 'it is not for a human being that Allah speak to him except by revelation, i.e. by revealing or by sending', he must imply his saying «أو من وراء حجاب» in an implied form that corresponds to them, such as «أو أن يسمع من وراء حجاب». It has been read «أو يرسل رسولا فيوحي» with raising, on 'or He sends', or in the sense of «مرسلا», conjoined to «وحيا» in the sense of «موحيا»."
As for the wording of al-Samīn: "Nāfiʿ read «يرسل» with raising of the lām, and likewise «فيوحي» with its yāʾ silent; the rest read it with the accusative. As for the first reading, it has three aspects:
1- One: it is raised by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. «أو هو يرسل».
2- Two: it is conjoined to «وحيا» as a ḥāl, because «وحيا» is also in the construction of a ḥāl, as though He had said «إلا موحيا أو مرسلا».
3- Three: it is conjoined to what «من وراء» is attached to, since its implied form is «أو يسمع من وراء حجاب», and «وحيا» is in the position of a ḥāl, conjoined to that implied element, to which «أو يرسل» is conjoined, the implied form being «إلا موحيا أو مسمعا من وراء حجاب أو مرسلا».
As for the second reading, it has three aspects: 1- One: that it be conjoined to the implied element to which «من وراء حجاب» is attached, since its implied form is «أو يكلمه من وراء حجاب», and this implied verb is conjoined to «وحيا», and the meaning is «except by revelation, or making heard from behind a veil, or sending a messenger»; it is not permissible to conjoin it to «يكلمه» because of the corruption of the meaning. I say: for the implied form would become 'it is not for a human being that Allah send him as a messenger', which is corrupt in wording and meaning. Makkī said: because it would entail the negation of messengers and the negation of those sent to.
2- Two: that it be put in the accusative by an implied «أن», it and what it puts in the accusative being conjoined to «وحيا», and «وحيا» being a ḥāl, so it is here also a ḥāl, the implied form being «إلا موحيا أو مرسلا».
3- Three: that it be conjoined to the meaning of «وحيا», which is a maṣdar construed with «أن» and the verb, the implied form being «إلا بأن يوحى إليه أو بأن يرسل»; Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it.
As for his saying «أو من وراء حجاب»: the majority read it in the singular, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «حجب» in the plural; this preposition and its genitive noun is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being «أو يكلمه من وراء حجاب»; it has preceded that this verb is conjoined to the meaning of «وحيا», i.e. «إلا أن يوحي أو يكلمه». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «It is not permissible to attach «من» to the «يكلمه» present in the wording, because what comes before the exception does not act on what comes after «إلا»»; then he said: ««من» is attached to «يكلمه» because it is an adverbial, and latitude is allowed with adverbials.»"
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permissible that it be conjoined to «أن يكلمه», because its meaning would become 'it is not for a human being that Allah speak to him, nor that He send him a messenger', and that is corrupt."
2- Optional subjunctive of the imperfect verb: The imperfect verb is put in the accusative optionally by an implied «أن» after five particles: the prepositional lām, when it is not preceded by a negated past «kāna» (defective verb) and the verb is not joined with «لا»; if the lām is preceded by the said «kāna», the implying of «أن» is obligatory; and if the verb is joined with a negative or redundant emphatic «لا», showing it is obligatory so that two like letters, namely the lām of purpose and the lām of «لا», do not follow one another without assimilation, which is awkward in speech, as in «لئلا يكون للناس عليكم حجة» with the nūn assimilated into the negative «لا», and as in «لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب» with the nūn assimilated into the redundant emphatic «لا»; and this lām is called the lām of purpose (lām kay), the lām of consequence and the lām of emphasis. The four remaining particles of the five after which «أن» is implied optionally are: «الواو», «أو», «ثم» and «الفاء», when the conjunction by them is upon a noun not construed with a verb, and it is of two kinds, a maṣdar and other than a maṣdar. Other than a maṣdar is like the saying of Ḥuṣayn ibn Humām al-Murrī:
ولولا رجال من رزام أعزة ... وآل سبيع أو أسوءك علقما
(Were it not for mighty men of Rizām and the family of Subayʿ, or I would grieve you, O ʿAlqama.)
«فأسوءك» is conjoined to «رجال», which is not construed with a verb; Rizām is a clan of Numayr, and «علقما» is a vocative with its end shortened (murakhkham). The maṣdar is like «وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا أو من وراء حجاب أو يرسل رسولا» in the reading of other than Nāfiʿ with the accusative by an implied «أن» after «أو», the implied form being «إلا وحيا أو إرسالا», and «وحيا» is a maṣdar not construed with a verb; and the saying of Maysūn bint Baḥdal al-Kilābiyya, wife of Muʿāwiya ibn Abī Sufyān and mother of his son Yazīd:
ولبس عباءة وتقرّ عيني ... أحبّ إليّ من لبس الشفوف
(To wear a cloak and have my eye cool is dearer to me than wearing fine garments.)
«تقر» is put in the accusative by an implied «أن» optionally, and it and the verb are construed as a nominative maṣdar by conjunction upon «لبس» with the conjunctive wāw, on her words before it:
لبيت تخفق الأرواح فيه ... أحبّ إليّ من قصر منيف
(A house in which the winds flutter is dearer to me than a lofty palace.)
It is said «قرت عينه تقر» when its tears are rare, and that occurs only in joy, and it is derived from «القر» (cold); and it is said «سخنت» when its tears are hot, and that occurs only in sorrow. And his saying:
لولا توقع معتر فأرضيه ... ما كنت أوثر أترابا على أتراب
(Were it not for the expectation of a petitioner whom I would satisfy, I would not prefer some peers over others.)
«فأرضيه» is put in the accusative by an implied «أن» optionally after the fāʾ; «أن» and «أرضي» are construed as a maṣdar conjoined to «توقع», the implied form being «لولا توقع معتر فإرضائي إياه», and «توقع» is not construed with a verb; the «معتر» is the one who exposes himself to kindness, and the «أتراب» is the plural of «ترب» with kasra on the tāʾ, the one born with you at the time you were born and so equal to you in age; and the meaning is: were it not for expecting one who is turned away from doing kindness, and satisfying him, the poet would not have preferred one equal to others in age over one equal to him in his age. And the saying of Anas ibn Mudrika al-Khathʿamī:
إني وقتلي سليكا ثم أعقله ... كالثور يضرب لما عافت البقر
(I, and my killing Sulayk and then paying his blood-money, am like the bull that is struck when the cows refuse the water.)
«أعقله» is the imperfect of «عقل», put in the accusative by an implied «أن» optionally after «ثم»; «أن» and «أعقله» are construed as a maṣdar conjoined to «قتلي», the implied form being «وقتلي سليكا ثم عقلي إياه», and «قتلي» is not construed with a verb; «سليكا», a diminutive, is the name of a man, the object of «قتلي»; «كالثور» is the khabar of «إن»; by «الثور» is meant the male of the cattle, because the cattle follow him, so when he refuses the water they refuse it, and he is struck so that he goes to the water and they go with him; «أعقله» is from "I paid the blood-money for the slain man": I gave his diya. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ has an interesting opinion about the bull; he said it is the "bull of the algae", the one that rises above the water, so the cattle turn away from it, and so the owner of the cattle strikes it to clear the water and drink it; he said: he named it "bull" and mentioned it with the cattle to make a riddle of it for the hearer; but this is sheer affectation, and the first is correct.
